title: Subgroup unipotence, ind-unipotence and augmentation-power annihilation
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $G$ a topological group and $H$ a subgroup. Work in the category of $R$-linear $G$-representations $M$ with open stabilizers of all elements, with equivariant linear maps. Define $H$-unipotence to mean the existence of a finite increasing filtration $0=F_0M\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_nM=M$ by $G$-stable $R$-submodules with $\rho(h)m-m\in F_iM$ for every $h\in H$ and $m\in F_{i+1}M$. Define $H$-ind-unipotence to mean being a small filtered colimit in that category of $H$-unipotent objects. The augmentation $R[H]\to R$ sends every $[h]$ to $1$; define $I_H$ as its kernel, regarded as an $R$-submodule, and its powers by $I_H^0=R[H]$ and $I_H^{q+1}=I_H I_H^q$, using the $R$-span of products. Define $I_H^qm=0$ to mean that every $a\in I_H^q$ acts as zero on $m$, via the algebra homomorphism extending $\rho|_H$. The length-zero filtration is allowed.
